firststeps.title: First steps
firststeps.welcome: Ascended Tweaks shows every change beforehand, backs up every affected value and can undo everything. The app sends no data.
firststeps.disclaimer: You make changes to your system at your own responsibility. The app creates backups but cannot guarantee every configuration. Please note these limits:
firststeps.baseline: The app now records the original state of every location it can change. Nothing is changed.
firststeps.baseline.exists: The original state is already saved.
firststeps.restorepoint: Optional: create a Windows restore point. Windows will ask for administrator rights.
settings.expert.help: Shows tweaks with risk "Expert" and evidence "Disputed".
restore.backups.empty: No backups yet. They are created on the first apply and when the original state is saved.
dryrun.norestorepoint: No Windows restore point is created for user settings (that would require administrator rights). Ascended Tweaks' own backup is enough to undo everything.
perm.title: Permission overview
perm.intro: Which apps may use the camera, microphone and location? Display only: change this in Windows Settings.
perm.error: The overview could not be read: {error}
autostart.intro: Programs that start after sign-in. “Disable” keeps the entry and only turns off its approval, like Task Manager. Undo with “Enable again” or on the Restore page.
autostart.machine: for all users, administrator rights needed
autostart.reason.windows: Part of Windows. Do not change.
autostart.reason.security: Security program. Do not disable, otherwise protection starts later or not at all.
autostart.reason.driver: Driver or device program, needed for audio, graphics or input control. Do not change.
autostart.reason.updater: Updater or program launcher, uncritical. Updates then run when you open the program.
autostart.reason.microsoft: Program from Microsoft. Only disable it if you do not need it right after sign-in.
autostart.reason.known: Program from a known publisher (valid signature). Disabling is uncritical if you do not need it right after sign-in.
autostart.reason.unsigned: Unclear origin (no valid signature). Do not change, check first.
autostart.reason.missing: The file is missing, the entry is orphaned. Do not change, check first.
autostart.readonly.task: Task of another program: display only.
autostart.readonly.runonce: Runs only a single time: display only.
autostart.disabled.external: Disabled outside Ascended Tweaks, for example in Task Manager.
services.intro: Only services from the verified catalog, no bulk list. Changes are made with the card in “Settings” (disputed ones in expert mode).
tasks.intro: Only scheduled tasks from the verified catalog. Changes are made with the card in “Settings”.
processes.intro: Display only: the 15 programs using the most memory and the most processor time. Windows uses free memory as a cache; “clean RAM” brings no lasting benefit and is deliberately missing.
gaming.anticheat.notice: Anti-cheat systems such as Vanguard, EasyAntiCheat and BattlEye check security features like Secure Boot, TPM and memory integrity. This app never turns these features off automatically. Turning off memory integrity is only possible as an expert option, lowers the protection of your system and can cause games or anti-cheat services to refuse the connection.
gaming.profiles.intro: Per game you can set the GPU preference, fullscreen optimization and starting with high priority. "Apply" shows the preview first; everything can be undone on the Restore page.
gaming.profiles.empty: No game profiles yet. Add a detected game or choose an EXE.
gaming.profile.gpu: Prefer the "High performance" graphics card (only with more than one graphics card)
gaming.profile.fso: Fullscreen optimizations off for this game (disputed effect, test per game)
gaming.profile.priority: Set priority "High" when started through Ascended Tweaks (this session only)
gaming.profile.permanent.locked: Permanent priority is blocked for games with anti-cheat.
gaming.detected.pickexe: The launcher names no EXE; you choose it when adding.
gaming.start.PriorityDenied: Started, but Windows or the anti-cheat does not allow changing the priority. This is not bypassed.
gaming.start.GameNotFound: The game was not found or did not start within two minutes.
anticheat.intro: Display only. Shows which security features are active that anti-cheat systems often check. Some anti-cheat systems require Secure Boot and TPM.
anticheat.explain.secureboot: Starts Windows only with signed boot components. Some anti-cheat systems require Secure Boot. It can only be turned on in the computer's UEFI setup.
anticheat.explain.tpm: Security chip for keys and boot measurements. Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0; so do some anti-cheat systems.
anticheat.explain.hvci: Protects the kernel against tampered drivers. Some anti-cheat systems require it. Turning it off is only possible as an expert option (GAME-019).
anticheat.explain.vbs: Basis for memory integrity. Not changed by Ascended Tweaks.
anticheat.explain.testsigning: Allows unsigned drivers. If it is on, anti-cheat systems often refuse to start. Turn it off with administrator rights through bcdedit; Ascended Tweaks does not change it.
anticheat.explain.kerneldebug: An active kernel debugger often makes anti-cheat systems abort. Ascended Tweaks does not change it.
clean.intro: Scan first, then select, then clean. Deleted files cannot be restored through Ascended Tweaks. In Recycle Bin mode you get them back from the Recycle Bin; for system folders deletion is always permanent.
clean.estimated: Estimated without administrator rights; protected files are missing from the total.
clean.blocked.browser: Please close {name} first. Otherwise this area is skipped.
clean.confirm.title: Really clean?
clean.confirm.noundo: Deleted files cannot be restored through Ascended Tweaks.
clean.confirm.admin: For system folders Windows asks for administrator rights.
clean.result.title: Cleanup finished
clean.result.recycled: {n} files moved to the Recycle Bin ({size}).
clean.result.inuse: {n} files were in use and were skipped.
clean.CLEAN-001.name: Temporary files (user)
clean.CLEAN-001.desc: Files in your account's temp folder that are older than one day. Open files stay.
clean.CLEAN-001.side: Running installations could miss files if they have been open for more than a day; hence the age limit.
clean.CLEAN-002.name: Temporary files (Windows)
clean.CLEAN-002.desc: Files in C:\Windows\Temp older than one day. Open files stay.
clean.CLEAN-003.name: Windows Update leftovers
clean.CLEAN-003.desc: Downloaded update packages. The update services are stopped briefly and restored exactly as before afterwards.
clean.CLEAN-003.side: Updates not installed yet are downloaded again.
clean.CLEAN-004.name: Delivery Optimization cache
clean.CLEAN-004.desc: Cached update parts of Delivery Optimization.
clean.CLEAN-004.side: Other devices on the network can no longer get these parts from this PC.
clean.CLEAN-005.name: Previous Windows installation
clean.CLEAN-005.desc: The Windows.old folder, removed through the official Windows Disk Cleanup.
clean.CLEAN-005.side: Going back to the previous Windows version is no longer possible afterwards.
clean.CLEAN-006.name: Empty Recycle Bin
clean.CLEAN-006.desc: Empties the Recycle Bin of all drives.
clean.CLEAN-006.side: Files in the Recycle Bin are gone for good afterwards.
clean.CLEAN-007.name: Thumbnails
clean.CLEAN-007.desc: Cache of the preview images in File Explorer. Files in use stay.
clean.CLEAN-007.side: Thumbnails are recreated the next time a folder is opened; that takes a moment.
clean.CLEAN-008.name: Error reports
clean.CLEAN-008.desc: Sent and queued Windows error reports.
clean.CLEAN-008.side: Reports not sent yet are lost.
clean.CLEAN-009.name: Crash dumps
clean.CLEAN-009.desc: Memory dumps after crashes (Minidump, MEMORY.DMP, LiveKernelReports).
clean.CLEAN-009.side: The cause of past crashes can no longer be investigated afterwards.
clean.CLEAN-010.name: Chrome cache
clean.CLEAN-010.desc: Google Chrome caches (Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache) of all profiles. Never cookies, passwords, history or bookmarks.
clean.CLEAN-010.side: Pages load a little slower the first time. Chrome must be closed.
clean.CLEAN-011.name: Edge cache
clean.CLEAN-011.desc: Microsoft Edge caches (Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache) of all profiles. Never cookies, passwords, history or favorites.
clean.CLEAN-011.side: Pages load a little slower the first time. Edge must be closed.
clean.CLEAN-012.name: Firefox cache
clean.CLEAN-012.desc: Firefox cache (cache2) of all profiles. Never cookies, passwords, history or bookmarks.
clean.CLEAN-012.side: Pages load a little slower the first time. Firefox must be closed.
clean.CLEAN-013.name: Shader caches
clean.CLEAN-013.desc: Cached shaders of DirectX and the graphics drivers (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel). Helps with display errors but does not raise the frame rate.
clean.CLEAN-013.side: The first starts of games stutter until the shaders are rebuilt.
clean.CLEAN-014.name: Component store
clean.CLEAN-014.desc: Removes superseded system components with DISM /StartComponentCleanup. Only DISM itself determines the size; that can take a few minutes.
clean.CLEAN-014.side: Some installed updates can no longer be uninstalled afterwards.
debloat.intro: Remove preinstalled apps for all users. Nothing is preselected. Removed apps are listed on the Restore page; restoring tries to re-register and otherwise opens the Store page. Not every restore is guaranteed.
debloat.deprovision: Also remove for new user accounts (provisioned package)
debloat.locked: System app: needed by Windows and cannot be removed here.
debloat.warning.vendor: Probably driver, device or security software. Only remove it if you are sure.
debloat.confirm.title: Remove apps?
debloat.confirm.restore: Restoring tries to re-register, otherwise it opens the Store page. Not every restore is guaranteed. Windows asks for administrator rights.
debloat.confirm.deprovision: The provisioned package is removed too: new user accounts no longer get the apps.
debloat.result.title: Apps removed
onedrive.intro: OneDrive is only uninstalled if no data can be lost. If Desktop, Documents or Pictures are redirected to OneDrive or there are files that are only available online, uninstalling is blocked.
onedrive.ready: No obstacles found. OneDrive can be uninstalled.
onedrive.blocked: Uninstall blocked so that no data is lost:
onedrive.confirm.title: Uninstall OneDrive?
onedrive.confirm.body: OneDrive is uninstalled for your account. The files in the OneDrive folder stay on the PC but are no longer synced. Ascended Tweaks cannot reinstall OneDrive automatically; use OneDriveSetup.exe in the Windows folder or the download from Microsoft.
onedrive.block.KnownFolderMove: These folders are in OneDrive: {folders}. First stop the backup in OneDrive under Settings > Sync and backup > Manage backup.
onedrive.block.OnlineOnlyFiles: {n} files are only available online. First download the folders with right-click > "Always keep on this device".
onedrive.block.ScanIncomplete: Too many files to check safely. Blocked as a precaution.
onedrive.block.MachineWide: OneDrive is installed for all users. Please uninstall it through Settings > Apps.
onedrive.block.SetupNotTrusted: The uninstaller is not validly signed by Microsoft. Blocked for security reasons.

restore.apps.note: Restore tries to re-register the package that is still present and otherwise opens the Store page. Not every restore is guaranteed.
restore.apps.outcome.StoreOpened: Re-registration was not possible; the Store page was opened.
restore.apps.outcome.Failed: Restore not possible, and the Store page could not be opened either.

net.doh.title: DNS over HTTPS

updates.info: Windows Update is never turned off permanently. Security updates close vulnerabilities that are actively exploited. Here you can defer or pause updates or control restarts; after a pause, Windows resumes updates by itself.
updates.status.title: Status
updates.pause.intro: Pauses feature and quality updates for at most 35 days. No security updates arrive during the pause. You can also do this in Windows Settings.
updates.expertonly: Pausing directly from Ascended Tweaks is "Disputed" (the values are not documented) and only available in expert mode. Without expert mode: "Open Windows Update" and pause there.
profiles.intro: A profile is a list of tweaks with a target state. Before applying, you see what changes and what is skipped; afterwards, a before-and-after comparison. Imported profiles are checked and only applied when you press the button.
profiles.plan.summary: {apply} to apply, {revert} to reset, {unchanged} already in target state, {skip} skipped
profiles.skip.unavailable: Skipped: not available on this system
profiles.skip.foreign: Skipped: not set by Ascended Tweaks, will not be reset
profiles.save.title: Save profile
profiles.rename.title: Rename profile

profiles.name.invalid: 1 to 60 characters, no control characters and no spaces at the start or end.
profiles.save.empty: No tweak is active; there is nothing to save.
profiles.delete.title: Delete profile
profiles.delete.body: The profile "{name}" will be deleted. Applied tweaks stay unchanged.
profiles.import.done: Profile checked and imported. Review the preview before applying it.
profiles.compare.title: Before and after
profiles.metric.title: Measurements
profiles.metric.disk: Free space on the system drive
profiles.metric.note: Snapshots right before and after applying. Memory use changes constantly; some tweaks only take effect after a restart.
dashboard.indicators.intro: Only measurable values with an explanation. There is deliberately no overall score.
dashboard.ind.autostart.why: Programs that start when you sign in. Each one costs some time and memory at startup.
dashboard.ind.free.why: Little free space can make updates fail.
dashboard.ind.ramload.why: Snapshot. Windows uses free memory as a cache; a high value is not automatically bad.
dashboard.ind.reboot.why: Updates or installations only finish after a restart.
dashboard.ind.trim.why: Tells SSDs which blocks are free; keeps write performance up over time.
dashboard.ind.secureboot.why: Only allows signed boot loaders at startup. Some anti-cheat systems require Secure Boot and TPM.
dashboard.ind.tpm.why: Security chip for keys, for example for BitLocker and Windows Hello.
dashboard.ind.hvci.why: Protects the Windows kernel from tampered drivers.
dashboard.ind.gamemode.why: Windows prioritizes running games and holds back update restarts. Default: on.
dashboard.ind.defender.why: Display only. If another antivirus is active, Defender steps back by itself. Ascended Tweaks does not change this.
profiles.script.done: {n} tweaks exported as a PowerShell script (and .reg where possible), each with a reset script. {skipped} tweaks only work in the app; they are listed at the top of the file.
settings.update.help: Only when you press the button, never automatically. The request contains no data about you or your PC. An update only starts if signature, checksum and publisher match and you agree.
settings.update.notconfigured: Update checking is not set up in this version yet (address, key and certificate are not decided yet).
settings.update.ready.body: Version {version} was downloaded and verified (signature, checksum, publisher). The installer starts now and asks for administrator rights.
settings.logs.help: Only on this PC, nothing is sent. User name and profile path are replaced. Logs of the helper service are under %ProgramData% and can only be deleted with administrator rights.
settings.logs.delete.body: All log files of this user are deleted. Backups and applied tweaks stay unchanged.
settings.logs.inuse: {n} files are in use and were not deleted.
settings.cli.body: For scripts, {exe} is in the program folder, with the same engine and the same safety rules. Examples: --list --module PRIV, --profile safe --dry-run, --export ps1 --profile safe --out C:\Export\safe.ps1. Expert and disputed tweaks need --allow-expert there; the administrator prompt cannot be bypassed.
settings.reset.help: Language and expert mode back to default. Applied tweaks, backups and profiles stay unchanged.
settings.reset.body: Language and expert mode are set to default. Applied tweaks stay as they are.
about.title: About Ascended Tweaks
about.disclaimer: Changes to the system are made at your own risk. The app creates backups but cannot guarantee every configuration.
about.privacy: We collect nothing. No accounts, no telemetry, no ads. Logs stay on your PC. The only network access comes from functions you start yourself: latency test, DNS test, update check.
about.trademark: Windows is a trademark of Microsoft Corporation. This software is not affiliated with Microsoft, Epic Games or any other company mentioned.
mode.title: View
simple.search: What would you like to improve?
simple.start.status: Your PC: {windows}, {ram} memory, {n} programs start with Windows.
simple.start.help: A preset combines several settings. Before applying, you see every change. Under Undo you can take everything back.
simple.faster.help: These settings make Windows start or respond faster. Noticeable means the effect is proven and you will feel it. Small means proven but hardly noticeable.
simple.gaming.help: Settings for games, for example without mouse acceleration. Nothing here promises more FPS; some settings make controls more precise.
simple.privacy.help: These settings send less data to Microsoft and show fewer ads. They do not make the PC faster.
simple.back.help: Here is everything Ascended Tweaks changed. You can undo each entry on its own, or everything at once at the top.
simple.back.empty: Ascended Tweaks has not changed anything yet.
simple.autostart.title: Programs at startup
simple.autostart.intro: Every program here starts with Windows. You can turn off what you do not need right away; the program stays installed.
simple.ping.title: Check internet
simple.ping.intro: Measures how fast and steady your internet responds. Changes nothing.
simple.updates.title: Updates
simple.updates.intro: Updates close security holes. You can pause them in Windows Update.
glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.autostart.text: Programs that start by themselves after you sign in. Many of them are not needed right away.
glossary.dns.text: The service that turns web addresses like example.com into numbers so your PC can find the site.
glossary.cache.text: Stored files that help programs load faster. They are created again when needed.
glossary.registry.text: The central settings database of Windows. Ascended Tweaks backs up every value before changing it.
glossary.service.text: A program that works in the background for Windows, for example for printing.
glossary.backup.text: The old state of each setting before Ascended Tweaks changes it. That is why Undo always works.
glossary.restorepoint.text: A backup made by Windows itself. It helps if the PC no longer starts properly after a change.
glossary.admin.text: Some settings apply to the whole PC. For those, Windows asks for your permission.

preset.safe.desc: Proven, safe settings for a faster, calmer PC.
preset.gaming.name: Gaming

preset.competitive.desc: Everything from Gaming and more for shooters like Fortnite. Never security features.
preset.laptop.name: Laptop Battery
preset.laptop.desc: Less background, power plan stays at default so the battery lasts.
preset.privacy.name: Privacy
preset.privacy.desc: Less data to Microsoft and fewer ads. Side effects are shown in the preview.
preset.cleanup.name: Clean Up
preset.cleanup.desc: Deletes temp files, caches and update leftovers. Changes no settings.
preset.office.name: Quiet Office
preset.office.desc: Fewer notices and suggestions, file extensions visible, no restart during the day.
level.title: Level
simple.preset.nothing: Everything in this preset is already set.
simple.preset.undo.nothing: This preset has nothing left to reset; other presets still need these settings.
simple.preset.cleanup.nothing: There is nothing to clean up right now.
simple.preset.alldone: Everything is already set, nothing to do.
clean.CLEAN-015.name: Discord cache
clean.CLEAN-015.desc: Discord cache folders (Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache). Never sign-in, settings or messages.
clean.CLEAN-015.side: Images and emojis load again on the next start. Discord must be closed.
clean.CLEAN-016.name: Spotify cache
clean.CLEAN-016.desc: Contents of the Spotify "Storage" folder (cache). What Spotify keeps there is not documented, hence "Caution".
clean.CLEAN-016.side: Spotify loads data again when playing. Spotify must be closed.
clean.CLEAN-017.name: Epic launcher web cache
clean.CLEAN-017.desc: Cache of the web views in the Epic Games Launcher (webcache, cache folders only). Never games, sign-in or cookies.
clean.CLEAN-017.side: Store pages load a little slower the first time. The launcher must be closed.
clean.CLEAN-018.name: Steam browser cache
clean.CLEAN-018.desc: Cache of the built-in Steam browser (htmlcache, cache folders only). Never games, saves or sign-in.
clean.CLEAN-018.side: Store and community load a little slower the first time. Steam must be closed.
clean.CLEAN-019.name: Teams cache (classic)
clean.CLEAN-019.desc: Cache of classic Microsoft Teams (Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache). New Teams is not touched.
clean.CLEAN-019.side: Teams loads images again. Teams must be closed.
clean.CLEAN-020.name: Program crash dumps
clean.CLEAN-020.desc: Memory dumps of crashed programs in "CrashDumps" (.dmp only, older than one day).
clean.CLEAN-020.side: The dumps only help developers analyze crashes; afterwards they are gone.
autostart.known.AUTO-001: Steam: game launcher. Starts Steam with its update check at sign-in; games also start without autostart.
autostart.known.AUTO-002: Epic Games Launcher: loads store and updates at startup. For Fortnite it is enough to open the launcher when needed.
autostart.known.AUTO-003: Discord: chat and voice channels. Without autostart you see messages only once you open Discord.
autostart.known.AUTO-004: Battle.net: Blizzard launcher. Only needed if you play Blizzard games right after startup.
autostart.known.AUTO-005: EA app: EA launcher. Also starts when you open an EA game.
autostart.known.AUTO-006: Ubisoft Connect: Ubisoft launcher. Starts with the game when needed.
autostart.known.AUTO-007: Spotify: music. Without autostart you simply open Spotify yourself.
autostart.known.AUTO-008: Microsoft Teams: chat and meetings. Without autostart you miss calls until Teams is open.
autostart.known.AUTO-009: OneDrive: syncs files with the cloud. Without autostart syncing starts only once you open OneDrive.
autostart.known.AUTO-010: Adobe updater: checks for Acrobat or Reader updates. Updates then arrive when you open the program.
process.known.memorycompression: Compressed memory of Windows. Normal and useful.
process.known.session: Windows sign-in and session. Do not touch.
process.known.services: Windows service control. Do not touch.
process.known.svchost: Host process for Windows services. It is normal to have many.
process.known.lsass: Windows security and sign-in. Do not touch.
process.known.explorer: Windows Explorer: taskbar, Start menu, folder windows.
process.known.dwm: Desktop Window Manager: draws all windows.
process.known.shell: Part of the Windows interface (Start, input, notifications).
process.known.wmi: Windows management (WMI), also used by programs.
process.known.webview: Web view inside programs (Microsoft Edge WebView2).
check.title: Gaming checks
check.intro: Display only: the checks change nothing. Each hint says how to fix it yourself.
check.refresh.title: Refresh rate
check.refresh.low: Your display can do {max} Hz but runs at {current} Hz. This is the most common reason for a choppy picture.
check.refresh.ok: Your display runs at {current} Hz, its maximum.
check.refresh.howto: Settings > System > Display > Advanced display: choose the highest refresh rate.
check.power.title: Power plan
check.power.saver: Windows runs in power saver mode and throttles the processor.
check.power.howto: Settings > System > Power & battery: power mode "Balanced" or "Best performance".
check.hybrid.title: Graphics in a laptop
check.hybrid.yes: Your laptop has two graphics chips. Games may run on the weaker, power-saving one.
check.hybrid.no: No laptop with two graphics chips detected.
check.hybrid.howto: Settings > System > Display > Graphics: choose "High performance" for the game, or create a game profile in Ascended Tweaks.
check.ramspeed.title: Memory speed
check.ramspeed.low: Memory runs at {configured} instead of {rated} (value of the modules).
check.ramspeed.ok: Memory runs at {configured}, as the modules state.
check.ramspeed.howto: Check the memory profile (XMP or EXPO) in the BIOS. This differs by mainboard; only change it if you know what you are doing.
check.ramcount.title: Memory modules
check.ramcount.howto: Two modules (dual channel) are often faster. This is a hint, not a buying recommendation.
check.disk.title: Space on the system drive
check.disk.low: Only {percent}% free. With little space, updates and games get slower.
check.disk.howto: Free up space under "Clean up" in Ascended Tweaks.
check.gamemode.title: Game Mode
check.gamemode.howto: Settings > Gaming > turn on Game Mode. Game Bar and capture are on the same page.
check.driver.title: Graphics driver
check.driver.old: The driver for {name} is about {months} months old.
check.driver.ok: The driver for {name} is less than a year old.
check.driver.howto: Get the current driver from the vendor page. Ascended Tweaks downloads nothing.
check.background.title: Background
check.background.top: {n} programs start with Windows. Largest user right now: {name} ({mb} MB).
check.anticheat.title: Secure Boot, TPM, memory integrity
check.anticheat.attention: At least one item can cause problems with some anti-cheat systems.
check.anticheat.howto: Details are in the "Anti-cheat" section, including what you can check yourself.
measure.title: Measurement
measure.none: No measurement yet. Measure now to see what changed after a preset.
measure.after.reboot: Preset applied. After the next restart you can "Measure after".
measure.note: Single measurements vary. Data is stored only on this PC.
large.intro: Shows only what can sensibly go. Games, programs and Windows never appear here for deletion. Files only go to the Recycle Bin.
large.done: Done: {a} can usually go, {b} please check, {hidden} protected.
large.truncated: Too many files, the search stopped early: {a} can usually go, {b} please check, {hidden} protected.
large.timeout: Time limit of 90 seconds reached, partial result: {a} can usually go, {b} please check, {hidden} protected.
large.protected.intro: Probably keep, games and system areas: view only, never delete.
large.confirm.title: Move to Recycle Bin?
large.confirm.body: {n} files, {size} in total. Largest: {largest}. Really move to the Recycle Bin?
large.skip.missing: Skipped: the file no longer exists.
large.skip.changed: Skipped: the file changed since the search.
large.why.installer: Installer or archive in Downloads, unchanged for {days} days.
large.why.cache: File in a cache folder, unchanged for {days} days.
large.why.oldvideo: Large video in Downloads, Desktop or Temp, unchanged for {days} days.
large.why.oldarchive: Large archive in Downloads, Desktop or Temp, unchanged for {days} days.
large.why.recent: Changed in the last {days} days, probably still needed.
large.why.library: In Documents, Pictures, Videos or Music.
large.why.keeptype: Database, virtual machine, mail archive or password file.
large.why.cloud: Stored in the cloud (online only); never downloaded or deleted.
large.why.unknown: Unknown file; not offered for deletion to be safe.
large.why.system: Part of Windows or an installed program.
large.games.title: Storage per game
large.games.intro: Ascended Tweaks never deletes games. To remove one, uninstall it in its launcher or in Windows apps.
keep.title: Always keep (large files)
keep.intro: The large file search never shows these files and folders again.
simple.clean.intro: Caches and leftovers that Windows and programs recreate. Personal files are not included.
simple.clean.note: Where possible, everything goes to the Recycle Bin. You see what will be deleted first.
install.title: How do you want to use Ascended Tweaks?
install.body: Install puts Ascended Tweaks into your user folder, with Start menu and desktop entries and an entry in "Apps" for removal. No administrator rights are needed. Portable starts directly from this folder.
install.failed: Installing did not work: {error} Ascended Tweaks now starts portable.
install.uninstall.title: Remove Ascended Tweaks?
install.uninstall.body: Removes the program, the shortcuts and the entry in "Apps". Your Windows settings stay as they are; you can reset them first in Ascended Tweaks under "Undo".
install.uninstall.problems:
Ascended Tweaks was removed, but not everything could be deleted:
{problems}
install.uninstall.notinstalled: This copy is not installed. You can simply delete a portable folder.
firststeps.settingslater: You can change the language in Settings at any time.
install.message.title: Ascended Tweaks
